findings.reason: an implementation that merges the steerable fields onto a fresh `_queued_request_record` (as `queue_dispatch` does today) reproduces the incident for `argv` and `base_sha` while passing the test, because the test constructs its queued request without them.
findings.text: §17's Deliverable now says "They were lost because launch followed the repointed manifest path into a second run directory, so keeping the original `manifest_path` is what keeps them", but `argv` and `base_sha` are written by launch unconditionally into the request's own pointer (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3231` from the composed plan, `:2979` from the worktree) and never read from the manifest path; the write that removes them is `queue_dispatch`'s whole-record overwrite (`reckon/crew/runs.py:770`), which preserves only `run_id`, `queued_at` and `created_at`. A queued pointer can carry those fields: every internal re-queue goes through `_mutate_pointer` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3377`), so a request held and released after a launch attempt keeps its launched fields, and a coordinator re-dispatch of it wipes them again under the stated remedy.

findings.reason: the node's gate as written cannot pass without either a failing assertion or launch-time code outside the deliverable, so the node would chase a field this defect never lost at launch; the case should assert `argv`/`base_sha` from launch and take the session id through `observe`, which is the path whose absence made `crew resume` refuse.
findings.text: the third case requires "a live pointer carrying the `session_id`, `argv` and `base_sha` that launch writes", but `session_id` is written at launch as `reuse_session` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3023`), which is `None` for any run that does not continue a prior session, and the only writer of an observed session id is `dispatch_sessions.observe` (`:230`, `:290`), a separate call that folds the stream. A stub worker launched through the admission pass therefore leaves `session_id` null in the pointer, whatever the manifest path names.

findings.reason: the constant is the deliverable's single definition of steerable, so an omission there becomes a behaviour the node builds and the test does not exercise; a coordinator re-dispatching a briefed node would get the old authority without an error.
findings.text: the steerable set is enumerated as "goal, done-when, negative control, write paths, inputs, time budget and dispatch options", which omits `node.brief`, `node.brief_path` and `node.brief_sha256` that `_queued_request_record` stores and that `_launch_queued` reads (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:274-281`); a re-dispatch of a briefed queued node with a changed brief would therefore drop the new brief silently and launch the old one.
